diagnoses.label: amount_keyword_priority_vs_last_number_fallback_misapplied
diagnoses.general_pattern: When a receipt contains the primary keyword line (e.g., GRAND TOTAL / TOTAL) with the numeric amount on the SAME line, the extractor must take that number and must not fall back to the 'last number on the next line' rule. The two-line fallback is only valid when the keyword line itself has no number.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Selecting an unrelated nearby number (e.g., a trailing line's figure, a tax/GST amount, or an item unit price) instead of the number co-located with the highest-priority keyword, or applying the next-line fallback even when the keyword line already contains the amount.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: 077.jpg prediction total_amount=23.26 is marked incorrect; the receipt (Banh Mi Cafe) shows 'Total (Inclusive of GST): 23.26' and a bold 'TOTAL: 23.25' after rounding adjustment -0.01. The predicted value matched a non-final 'Total (Inclusive of GST)' line rather than the final bold TOTAL after rounding. 074.jpg prediction 702.00 is marked incorrect; the Thai Delicious receipt shows 'Total : 92.80' and 'Grand Total : 92.80' with Cash Received 100.00, so 702.00 is not any line's value and indicates a misassembled/concatenated OCR number was selected rather than the GRAND TOTAL line. Both are compute-stage selection errors over text, not OCR glyph errors on the digits themselves (prices are visible).
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: A deterministic priority-ladder pass that (1) scans OCR lines top-to-bottom, (2) picks the FIRST line matching the highest-available priority keyword that is not in the exclusion set, (3) extracts the LAST numeric token on that line with the pattern d{1,3}(,d{3})*(.d{2}) or d+.d{2}, and only (4) falls back to the next non-empty line's last numeric token when step 3 yields no number. The current flow instead appears to pick numbers by proximity/size heuristics without binding to the keyword ladder, and does not sanity-check the extracted token against a monetary regex (which would have rejected 702.00 as a mis-concat of two tokens on 074).
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Define a reusable receipt_total_extraction procedure in image-ocr SKILL.md: iterate the keyword priority list GRAND TOTAL > TOTAL RM/TOTAL: RM > TOTAL AMOUNT > TOTAL/AMOUNT/TOTAL DUE/AMOUNT DUE/BALANCE DUE/NETT TOTAL/NET TOTAL; skip any line whose normalized text contains SUBTOTAL/SUB TOTAL/TAX/GST/SST/DISCOUNT/CHANGE/CASH TENDERED; for the matched line take the last token matching a strict monetary regex; only if none, read the next line's last monetary token; format to exactly two decimals. Also, when multiple matches at the same priority exist, prefer the LAST occurrence (post-rounding 'TOTAL:' typically appears after 'Total (Inclusive of GST):').
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies only to receipt-style images processed via image-ocr for monetary total extraction after raw OCR text is obtained. Does not apply to arbitrary document OCR or to date extraction.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not fold this into openai-vision (vision-based extraction uses prompts), pdf (structured text already available), video-frame-extraction, or xlsx. Do not apply to non-receipt text extraction.
diagnoses.target_section: Add a new section 'Receipt Field Extraction (Totals)' under or adjacent to 'Multi-Pass OCR Strategy'

diagnoses.label: date_disambiguation_when_multiple_dates_present
diagnoses.general_pattern: Receipts frequently contain more than one date-like token (transaction date, print date, closing date, promotion date). The transaction/invoice date is the correct target; the extractor must bind to a date-labeled line or to the earliest/primary date and ignore 'PRINT', 'Closed', 'FRN ON', loyalty, or footer dates.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Picking the first or last date-like regex match without checking the surrounding label, causing selection of a secondary date (e.g., print timestamp or a nearby but unrelated date) when multiple dates are present.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: 034.jpg (Perniagaan Zheng Hui) prediction date=2018-08-09 is marked date_correct=false. The receipt displays 'Date: 09/03/2018' (DD/MM/YYYY => 2018-03-09) under 'Receipt #: CS00084670'. The predicted ISO value 2018-08-09 corresponds to interpreting '09/03/2018' as 2018-08-09 only if month/day are swapped AND the 03 is misread as 08, OR to a different token entirely; either way the extractor failed to bind to the labeled 'Date:' line with a MY-locale DD/MM/YYYY convention. 21/22 other receipts had correct dates, showing the general date routine works but fails specifically on multi-date / low-contrast cases without a label-binding step.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: A date-selection pass that (1) prefers lines whose normalized text contains 'DATE' or 'INVOICE DATE' and is not preceded by 'PRINT', 'CLOSED', 'FRN', 'LOYALTY'; (2) parses with DD/MM/YYYY as primary and DD-MM-YY/DD/MM/YY as secondary for Malaysian receipts; (3) when multiple candidates survive, picks the earliest in reading order on the first qualifying line.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Add a 'Receipt Date Extraction' subsection documenting the label-binding and DD/MM/YYYY-first convention, with explicit exclusion of PRINT/CLOSED/FRN/LOYALTY-prefixed date lines, then ISO-format the chosen date.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies to receipt-style OCR where multiple dates may appear and locale is predominantly DD/MM/YYYY. Does not apply to generic document OCR or to tasks where date locale is known to differ.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not push into openai-vision or pdf. Do not assume DD/MM for non-receipt tasks.

diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Implement a documented tiered keyword matcher in image-ocr/SKILL.md's receipt section: iterate keyword tiers in priority order; within a tier collect all lines, parse amounts tolerant to OCR noise (letters-as-digits like o/O→0, l/I→1, u→0, B→8, S→5), reconcile duplicates by majority / nearest‑to‑subtotal‑plus‑tax, and only move to the next tier if the current tier yields no parseable number. Skip exclusion‑keyword lines before matching.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies to receipt-style OCR tasks where the task prompt supplies an explicit, ranked list of total keywords and an exclusion list; applies at the text-to-field extraction step after OCR text is available.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not apply to generic document OCR tasks without a declared total-keyword hierarchy, to invoice tasks where 'Total' refers to pre-tax subtotal by convention, or to multi-currency documents where the keyword tier itself is ambiguous.

diagnoses.label: ocr_digit_corruption_on_chosen_total_line_not_repaired
diagnoses.general_pattern: Tesseract regularly maps digits to visually similar letters on receipts (0→o/O/u/D, 1→l/I/i, 2→Z, 5→S/s, 6→b/G, 8→B, 9→g); when the chosen total line contains such corruption, the extracted amount must be normalized/validated against neighboring numeric evidence before being written.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: The agent accepted the raw OCR substring '702.00' from a line that in the image reads '102.00' because the leading '1' was OCR'd as '7', without any sanity check against Subtotal/Payment/Rounded lines on the same receipt.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: 074.jpg OCR text block: 'Subtotal : 102.00', 'Tolalecl. of GST 96.23', 'Total inel. of GBT 702.00', 'Toial Amt Rounded oO yo2.00', 'Payment : 102.00'. The majority of parseable amounts cluster at 102.00; the prediction wrote 702.00. Field feedback amount_correct=false for 074.jpg confirms the chosen value disagrees with ground truth.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: A post-parse validation that (1) collects all numeric amounts from candidate total lines, (2) checks whether the chosen amount is approximately equal to subtotal+tax−discount±rounding or matches the modal 'Payment'/'Rounded Total' value, and (3) prefers the mode / arithmetic-consistent value when a single outlier differs by exactly one leading-digit substitution.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Add an 'OCR digit normalization and cross-check' step to image-ocr/SKILL.md: define a confusables map, re-parse the chosen total line with the map applied, then compare against (subtotal + tax - discount) and against other total-tier lines; if the chosen value is an outlier and a corrected candidate is arithmetically consistent, substitute it.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies only to receipt-like documents containing both a subtotal/tax breakdown and a single total; the arithmetic check is skipped when subtotal/tax are not confidently parsed.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not apply confusables substitution to free-form product-code or invoice-ID fields where digits and letters are semantically distinct, and do not override an unambiguous high-confidence total just because arithmetic is off by rounding.
diagnoses.target_section: new subsection 'Numeric Field Repair for Receipts' near 'Error Handling'

For receipts where total/date lines were visibly damaged by OCR (011.jpg '15.u00', 063.jpg '7B 02/18', 074.jpg '702.00'), the multi-pass strategy would have provided alternative hypotheses that the keyword/arithmetic check could choose from.

diagnoses.correct_general_approach: In image-ocr/SKILL.md's 'Multi-Pass OCR Strategy' section, add a trigger condition: 'If the chosen total line contains any non-[0-9.,] character inside the numeric span, or if arithmetic cross-check fails, re-run OCR with --psm 6 and ImageOps.autocontrast(grayscale) and reparse before committing the value.'
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies to receipt/invoice OCR where the target field is a short numeric string on a known-keyword line; the trigger is cheap (regex on the chosen line) so the extra pass is only paid when needed.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not run exhaustive 9-variant multi-pass OCR unconditionally for every image in large batches; cost grows linearly and the first pass is correct for the majority of clean receipts.

overlay.composition_issue: The image-ocr skill teaches generic OCR extraction and multi-pass strategy but contains no mechanism for structured field extraction from receipts: no priority keyword ladder, no exclusion-keyword handling, no numeric OCR normalization, no null-vs-empty-string convention, and no batch-consistent date parsing. Adding these receipt-oriented extraction mechanisms to image-ocr/SKILL.md and a short null-cell note to xlsx/SKILL.md directly addresses the observed amount and date failures (3/22 amount wrong, 1/22 date wrong) without changing the preserved multi-pass OCR, PSM, or preprocessing content that is already correct.

Do not alter image-ocr's output JSON schema or confidence tiers; the new mechanisms operate on the extracted_text field.
Do not change xlsx/SKILL.md's formula/recalc workflow; only add a small 'Null vs Empty String' note.
Preserve the task's declared keyword tiers and exclusion-keyword list verbatim when documenting the priority matcher.
Keep diagnoses observable-evidence based; do not import oracle totals/dates into the skill text.

diagnoses.label: amount_keyword_priority_resolution_misses_gst_summary_section
diagnoses.general_pattern: When applying priority-tiered keyword matching for monetary totals on OCR'd receipts, 'last line that matches' tie-breaking inside the lowest tier (TOTAL/AMOUNT) wrongly promotes 'Total' lines appearing inside a GST SUMMARY / TAX SUMMARY tabular section (e.g. 'a Total: 348.50', 'Total 16.71 0.99') over the true final payable total higher up (e.g. 'Total (RM): 332.30', 'Total After Adj Incl GST 17.70').
diagnoses.wrong_approach: The extraction script collects all lines matching generic TOTAL/AMOUNT patterns and simply takes candidates[-1] (the last textual occurrence), with exclusions only on narrow phrases like 'Total GST', '(GST|TAX|SST)\s+(TOTAL|SUMMARY|...)', and line-initial GST/TAX/SST. A line like 'a Total: 348.50' inside the GST summary block does not trigger any exclusion, so it wins over the real 'Total (RM): 332.30' line above.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Receipt 034.jpg produced total_amount='332.30' in the submitted xlsx, but the agent's own in-run debug trace shows the first extraction yielded 348.50 from the GST summary; receipt 071.jpg produced 17.70 after fixes but the first run printed total=0.99 from a 'Total 16.71 0.99' GST-summary row. These confirm the generic 'last TOTAL line' heuristic is pulling values from the GST/TAX summary section rather than the payment block.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: The skill never instructs the agent to treat 'GST SUMMARY' / 'TAX SUMMARY' as section headers that make all subsequent 'Total'/'Amount' lines ineligible candidates for the final payable total, nor to prefer the LAST non-summary total above such a section header.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: In the receipt-total selection step, maintain a section flag: once a line matching GST\s*SUMMARY / TAX\s*SUMMARY / SST\s*SUMMARY (or similarly '(?:GST|TAX|SST)\s+(?:Code|Rate|Amount)' column headers) is seen, exclude all subsequent lines from the TOTAL/AMOUNT candidate pool. Within the surviving candidates of the highest matched priority tier, prefer the last line; also iterate candidates in reverse so a candidate with no parseable number falls back to the previous one instead of giving up on the tier.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies only to receipt/invoice OCR extraction where a GST/TAX/SST summary block appears after the payment block and reuses words like 'Total' or 'Amount' as column labels; applies in the TOTAL/AMOUNT keyword tier selection step inside image-ocr-based receipt parsing.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not generalize to generic OCR text extraction, PDF table extraction, or non-receipt documents; do not change priority ordering of GRAND TOTAL > TOTAL RM > TOTAL AMOUNT > TOTAL defined by the task.
diagnoses.target_section: A new 'Receipt total selection: section-aware keyword priority' subsection under existing receipt/OCR guidance (or a 'Structured data extraction from receipts' addendum). Not under generic Tesseract Configuration or Preprocessing.

diagnoses.label: amount_extraction_fails_on_ocr_corrupted_digit_tokens
diagnoses.general_pattern: A strict decimal-money regex (\d+\.\d{1,2} / 1,234.56) silently drops totals when Tesseract substitutes letters for digits inside the amount token (e.g. '15.u00', '15.U0', '5.ug'), causing the candidate line to yield None and the whole priority tier to be abandoned without trying earlier candidates or correcting obvious OCR confusions.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: extract_last_number() applies NUM_RE strictly, and extract_total() only consults the single last candidate line per tier, then falls through to the next tier. There is no normalization of common OCR letter<->digit confusions (O/o/Q->0, l/I/|->1, S->5, B->8, Z->2, u/U->0 in digit context) and no backward iteration over multiple candidates in a tier before giving up.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: In the first script run the agent printed '011.jpg: ... total=None' and 'TOTAL 15.u00' appears in the agent's recorded OCR notes; the final submitted xlsx row for 011.jpg still shows total_amount='15.00' only after later patching, and 078.jpg shipped total_amount='' (empty) despite 'Grand Total 92.80' being visible in the receipt image and in agent OCR trace, consistent with a digit-token OCR corruption that was never normalized.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: The skill does not describe (a) targeted character normalization inside numeric-looking tokens prior to float parsing and (b) a per-tier backward scan over all candidate lines when the preferred candidate yields no parseable number.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Before applying the decimal regex, within tokens that match a 'mostly-digits with one or two confusable letters' shape near a currency keyword, substitute confusable glyphs (O/o/Q->0, l/I/|->1, S->5, B->8, Z->2, u->0) and retry; and in extract_total, iterate the collected candidates for the current tier in reverse order, returning the first that yields a parseable amount, rather than committing to candidates[-1] and only falling through to the next tier.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies specifically to parsing monetary amounts out of Tesseract OCR output on receipts; the letter->digit substitution is only safe inside tokens that are already dominated by digits/decimal points and sit on a line matching a TOTAL/AMOUNT keyword.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not apply letter->digit substitution to free text, product names, invoice IDs, dates, GST ID numbers, phone numbers, or any token not adjacent to a total/amount keyword; do not weaken the decimal/currency regex to accept arbitrary strings.
diagnoses.target_section: Same 'Receipt total selection' subsection, in a dedicated 'Numeric token normalization for OCR errors' and 'Per-tier backoff over multiple candidate lines' bullet.

diagnoses.label: amount_token_truncation_in_fuel_receipt_rm_line_mispicked_as_total_rm
diagnoses.general_pattern: The TOTAL RM priority tier matches any line containing 'TOTAL ... RM' and takes the last such line; on fuel receipts where a later 'Total Gross C RM 88.1' line has a truncated amount (missing final digit), the extractor prefers it over the earlier correct 'Total RM 88.17' or 'Total RN 88.17' line, producing an off-by-last-digit error.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Priority 2 pattern '\bTOTAL\s*:?\s*RM\b' plus candidates[-1] semantics unconditionally prefers the latest 'Total ... RM' match on the receipt, without checking that the amount token has the expected two-decimal structure or comparing against earlier same-tier amounts for consistency.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: In the agent's own first-run print, '064.jpg: date=2018-02-21, total=88.10' while the receipt clearly shows 'Total RM 88.17' three times; the agent's trace explicitly attributes this to 'Total Gross C RM 88.1' being chosen as the last Priority-2 match.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: The skill never instructs: when multiple candidate lines in the same tier yield amounts, prefer the amount whose decimal part has the full expected precision (two digits), and when amounts in the same tier agree (e.g. 88.17 appears on multiple 'Total ... RM' lines), prefer the agreeing value over an outlier whose decimal part is only one digit.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Within the TOTAL RM / TOTAL AMOUNT / TOTAL tiers, after collecting candidates compute all parseable amounts and (a) discard tokens whose decimal part has fewer than two digits when another candidate in the same tier offers a two-decimal amount, (b) if 2 or more candidates in the same tier produce the same amount, prefer that majority value over singletons, (c) otherwise fall back to the earlier policy. Also treat 'RN' as an OCR variant of 'RM' only in the priority pattern, not in exclusion patterns, so fuel receipts where Tesseract reads 'RN' still match the TOTAL RM tier.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies to receipt/invoice totals where OCR commonly truncates trailing digits or confuses 'RM'/'RN'; applies at the per-tier candidate ranking step.

diagnoses.label: date_extraction_too_brittle_for_degraded_fuel_receipts

diagnoses.wrong_approach: A single Tesseract pass on the raw image, with a strict date regex that requires clean '/','-' or '.' separators and 2 or 4-digit years, and no reattempt using the SKILL.md's documented preprocessing (grayscale+autocontrast, inversion, upscaling, PSM 6/4/11) specifically for the header region of the receipt.

The final shipped xlsx recovered some of these only after extra engineering, and the field_feedback shows 034.jpg date was still wrong (date_correct=false) despite correct amount.

diagnoses.correct_general_approach: When the first-pass OCR text yields no date match, invoke the multi-pass OCR path already described in SKILL.md on the top portion of the image (where receipt dates typically appear) with upscaling and PSM 6/11, and additionally run a tolerant date regex that permits 'I'/'l' as substitutes for '1' or '/' and accepts optional separators (DDMMYY glued forms) only when the resulting (day, month, year) triplet is calendar-valid.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies to extracting structured small fields (date, total) from degraded receipt images where single-pass Tesseract on the raw image fails; applies before giving up and writing null.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not generalize the tolerant date regex to free-form text or to non-receipt OCR tasks; do not use multi-pass OCR as the default (it is a fallback), and do not use it for product line items where its token merging would corrupt data.

diagnoses.label: writeback_null_total_written_as_empty_string_not_null

diagnoses.label: missing_summary_section_boundary_rule
diagnoses.general_pattern: When extracting a canonical total from receipt OCR text, lines occurring after a 'GST SUMMARY' / 'TAX SUMMARY' / 'Tax Code ... Amount ... Tax' header belong to a tax breakdown table and must not be considered candidates for the receipt total, even if they contain the token 'Total' or 'Amount'.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Treating every line containing 'TOTAL' or 'AMOUNT' as a candidate across the entire OCR text and using only line-local exclusion patterns like 'GST SUMMARY' on the same line, which fails when a later 'Total 16.71 0.99' or 'a Total: 348.50' row sits under a previously printed 'GST SUMMARY' header.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Trajectory a0012/a0014 shows 071.jpg producing total 0.99 from 'Total 16.71 0.99' under 'GST Summary Amount Tay'; 034 producing 348.50 from 'a Total: 348.50 8H' after 'GST SUMMARY'; 074 producing 96.23 via next-line fallback into 'SR gy a% 96.23 B77' after 'GST Summary Amount (RM) Tax (RM)'. Agent later had to invent SUMMARY_HEADER_RE in-run (a0022) to fix this.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Scan once for a summary-section header (GST SUMMARY / TAX SUMMARY / 'Amount (RM) Tax (RM)' / 'Tax Code') and restrict total-keyword candidate collection to lines strictly before that index.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Before applying priority tiers, locate the first summary-header line; only lines with index < summary_start are eligible candidates. Keep per-line exclusion patterns as a second filter for subtotals/tax/change/item-count.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies to receipt/invoice-style OCR text that contains a trailing GST/SST/VAT breakdown table; the eligible-region cutoff only governs total-amount candidate selection.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not apply this cutoff to date extraction, to non-receipt OCR documents, or to generic 'Amount' fields in tables where no summary header exists.
diagnoses.target_section: new subsection under 'Multi-Pass OCR Strategy' titled 'Domain pattern: receipt total disambiguation'

diagnoses.label: last_candidate_only_without_decimal_sanity
diagnoses.general_pattern: When multiple lines in the same priority tier contain the keyword, selecting strictly the last candidate without a sanity check on the extracted number (two-decimal monetary form) can latch onto item-count or truncated numbers (e.g., 'Total Item(s): 4', 'Total Gross C RM 88.1').
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Picking candidates[-1] and, if its line has no decimal number, blindly falling through to the next non-excluded line via a short-range fallback (which lands on tax-summary rows).
diagnoses.observable_evidence: In a0012/a0016 the agent traces that for 074 priority 4 picks 'Total Item(s): 4' (num=None) and then next-line fallback captures 96.23 from the SR row; for 009 the final 'TOTAL INCLUDES 6% GST' tail yields None causing total=None; for 064 'Total Gross C RM 88.1' is chosen over the earlier 'Total RN 88.17'.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Iterate candidates in reverse order; require the extracted number to match a monetary form (digits with exactly two decimals, optional thousands separators) before accepting; skip 'Total Item(s)/Qty/Savings' phrases as excluded.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: For each tier: collect candidates, iterate from last to first; a candidate is accepted only if its line yields a two-decimal number. The next-line fallback is used only when the current line has NO number at all, and the fallback line is itself non-excluded and inside the pre-summary region.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Within receipt total-amount extraction only; number-shape sanity is monetary (two decimals), not for arbitrary numeric fields.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not reject non-two-decimal numbers for date, invoice-number, quantity, or price-per-unit fields.
diagnoses.target_section: same 'Domain pattern: receipt total disambiguation' subsection

diagnoses.label: preprocessing_and_psm_not_defaulted_for_receipts
diagnoses.general_pattern: Thermal/scanned receipts are low-contrast and benefit strongly from grayscale + autocontrast preprocessing combined with Tesseract --psm 6 (uniform block). Using the default pytesseract.image_to_string on the raw PIL image loses digits (e.g., '15.u00' instead of '15.00', '702.00' instead of '102.00', '88.1' instead of '88.17').
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Calling pytesseract.image_to_string(Image.open(path)) with no preprocessing and no PSM, then trying to patch digit errors downstream via regex substitutions.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: a0013 vs a0017: raw OCR of 074 gives 'Total inel. of GBT 702.00' and 'Toial Amt Rounded oO yo2.00'; after grayscale+autocontrast+psm 6 the same image yields 'Total incl. of GST 102.00' and 'Date : 20/03/2018 13:01'. Similar gains on 011, 063, 064, 077, 083, 087, 088, 094.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: For receipt-like inputs, apply convert('L') + ImageOps.autocontrast and pass config='--psm 6' as the default pass before falling back to multi-pass strategies.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Document a 'receipt preset' in the OCR skill: grayscale, autocontrast, --psm 6, 300+ DPI; fall back to --psm 4/11 and inverted/sharpened variants only if the preset extraction fails downstream validation.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies specifically to printed receipt/invoice OCR with Tesseract; preset is a recommended starting point, not a mandate for all image types.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not force --psm 6 on sparse text, forms with multi-column layouts, or handwriting; do not autocontrast photographic images where it harms accuracy.
diagnoses.target_section: 'Image Preprocessing' / 'Tesseract Configuration Options' – add 'Receipt preset' note

diagnoses.label: duplicate_total_lines_tie_break_missing
diagnoses.general_pattern: Some receipts print both a verbose total ('Total (Inclusive of GST): 23.26') and a bare restated total ('TOTAL: 23.25') that may differ by rounding or OCR error. A naive last-match rule can prefer the less-reliable restatement.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Always take the lexically last TOTAL keyword line in the priority tier without considering phrase specificity or decimal consistency.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: a0017/a0018 shows 077.jpg producing two candidates 'Total (Inclusive of GST): 23.26' and 'TOTAL: 23.25'; the agent explicitly notes the ambiguity and settles on 23.25, which the field feedback marks as incorrect.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: When same-tier TOTAL candidates co-occur, prefer the one qualified by 'Inclusive of GST', 'Net Total', 'Rounded Total', 'Grand Total' over a bare 'TOTAL:' restatement; or prefer the earlier of two numerically close values when both are plausible.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Add a secondary ordering inside tier 4: qualified-TOTAL phrases outrank bare 'TOTAL:' phrases; among equally-qualified, use the last; treat a trailing bare 'TOTAL' line within 1-2 lines of the qualified total as a duplicate echo.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Only when multiple TOTAL candidates exist in the pre-summary region and all share the same priority tier.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not use this preference where only one TOTAL candidate exists, or when hints explicitly give a different priority (e.g., GRAND TOTAL already handled by tier 1).
diagnoses.target_section: 'Domain pattern: receipt total disambiguation' – tie-breaking rules

diagnoses.label: date_parsing_lenience_for_corrupted_separators
diagnoses.general_pattern: Receipt OCR frequently drops or substitutes date separators (e.g., '2032018' for '20/03/2018', '09/03/2018' for '08/09/2018'). A date extractor that only matches canonical DD/MM/YYYY, DD-MM-YYYY, or YYYY-MM-DD patterns will fail or capture a wrong-reading date.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Relying solely on strict separator-based regexes without a fallback that tries re-inserting separators after 8 consecutive digits or that cross-validates DD/MM/YY against known month ranges.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: a0017 shows 074 raw OCR 'Date : 2032018 13:01' versus preprocessed 'Date : 20/03/2018 13:01'; 063 raw 'pe /02/18' vs preprocessed '26/02/18'. Field feedback marks 034's date as incorrect while the amount is correct, consistent with an OCR-order ambiguity the skill does not address.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: After strict pattern matching fails, attempt a lenient parse: look for an 8-digit run near a 'Date' keyword and segment as DDMMYYYY / YYYYMMDD, validating month in 1..12 and day in 1..31; prefer dates near a 'Date' or 'Invoice' keyword.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Document in SKILL.md a two-stage date extractor: strict regex first, then a keyword-anchored lenient parser that reconstructs separators and validates ranges; always output ISO-8601 YYYY-MM-DD.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Receipt/invoice date fields anchored by a 'Date' keyword; not a general heuristic for timestamps embedded in free text.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not apply lenient 8-digit segmentation to arbitrary numeric strings like invoice/transaction IDs that happen to be 8 digits long.
diagnoses.target_section: new subsection 'Domain pattern: receipt date extraction'

diagnoses.label: within_tier_candidate_selection_last_wins_misses_true_total
diagnoses.general_pattern: When multiple keyword matches of the same priority tier appear (e.g., several lines containing bare TOTAL), picking the last occurrence as the amount can select a decorative/rounded/corrupted line (e.g., 'Total Amt Rounded ——S«702.00') over the semantically-correct earlier line (e.g., 'Total incl. of GST 102.00'). The rule needs cross-line consensus or a line-quality signal, not pure positional 'last'.

diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies only when total extraction is driven by hint-provided priority tiers over OCR text with multiple same-tier matches; does not alter OCR engine choice or date parsing.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not apply consensus override when a strictly higher-priority tier (e.g., GRAND TOTAL) matches cleanly; do not use it to override explicit exclusion keywords.

diagnoses.label: ocr_variant_selection_first_nonnull_without_quality_tiebreak
diagnoses.general_pattern: Running multiple OCR passes and accepting the first non-null extraction per field ignores that different passes have different per-field reliability. A later pass may yield a numerically more precise or more plausible value, but is discarded once an earlier pass produced any value.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Iterate OCR variants and break as soon as both date and total are non-None, keeping whichever came first.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: process_image loop: 'if date is None: date = extract_date(text); if total is None: total = extract_total(text); if date is not None and total is not None: break'. For 064.jpg the default pass returned 88.10 (OCR truncation) and loop exited before the preprocessed pass (which recovered 88.17) ran — fixed only by tightening NUM_RE, not by a principled variant arbitration.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Collect (tier, raw_decimal_string, value) from every OCR variant, then arbitrate across variants: prefer higher priority tier, then prefer values whose source string has exactly 2 fractional digits, then prefer values with cross-variant agreement, then prefer values consistent with Subtotal/Payment/Cash−Change identities.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Treat each OCR pass as producing candidate (tier, raw_number_string, value) tuples. Union them, then apply a documented arbitration order (tier → raw-decimal-precision → cross-variant agreement → consensus with other receipt lines). Never short-circuit on first non-null.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies when multiple OCR passes are run on the same image for the same structured field; does not require any specific preprocessing recipe.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Not a license to run unbounded preprocessing variants; the arbitration rule is independent of how many variants are produced.

diagnoses.label: monetary_number_regex_allowed_one_decimal_digit
diagnoses.general_pattern: Monetary amounts on receipts are reliably printed with exactly two fractional digits. A regex that accepts 1–2 fractional digits silently promotes OCR truncations like '88.1' to '88.10', hiding a known OCR failure mode and preventing fallback to a cleaner candidate.

diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Treat the two-decimal convention as a structural invariant for Malaysian/English receipt totals; require exactly two fractional digits in the money regex, and treat a one-decimal match as an OCR artifact to be rejected rather than padded.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Define the monetary number regex to require exactly two fractional digits (optionally with thousand separators), and only fall back to one-decimal or integer parsing as an explicitly flagged last-resort fallback.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies to total_amount extraction from receipt OCR text where the task output format itself specifies two decimal places.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Does not apply to generic numeric extraction from OCR (unit prices, quantities, percentages); only to the final monetary total field.

diagnoses.label: keyword_line_tier_matches_rounded_label_as_plain_total
diagnoses.general_pattern: A bare \bTOTAL\b keyword tier matches lines like 'Total Amt Rounded', 'Total GST', 'Total Excl. of GST', 'Total (Excluding GST)' when those lines are not explicitly on the exclusion list. These are not the final payable total and should be either excluded or routed to a lower tier.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Treating every line that contains the token TOTAL (and does not contain SUBTOTAL/TAX/GST/etc.) as a priority-4 total candidate.

diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not add exclusions that would drop legitimate 'GRAND TOTAL' or 'TOTAL RM' lines; refinements should be additive, not replace the given tiers.

diagnoses.label: date_parser_rejects_impossible_month_without_glyph_repair
diagnoses.general_pattern: When OCR confidently reads a date-shaped token but with an impossible component (month=62, day=32, year outside plausible range), downstream parsing returns None rather than attempting single-digit substitution against known OCR confusables (0↔6, 1↔7, 5↔S, 2↔Z) constrained to produce a valid date.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Parse the date token strictly; if any component is out of range, emit null.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: 071.jpg: OCR consistently reads '19/62/2018'; all PSM/preprocessing variants reproduce month 62. Agent noted true value is likely 19/02/2018 (0 misread as 6) but left the field null because no glyph-repair step exists.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: When a date-shaped token fails validation on exactly one numeric field, attempt bounded single-digit substitutions from a small OCR confusable table and accept the uniquely valid repair when it is also consistent with other date tokens found elsewhere in the OCR text.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Add an optional date-salvage pass: on validation failure, enumerate one-character substitutions from an OCR-confusable table; accept a repair only when (a) exactly one candidate validates and (b) its year/month/day fall in the plausible receipt range.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies to date parsing from receipt OCR where output is ISO date and OCR confusables are the dominant failure mode; off by default to avoid false positives when no plausible repair exists.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not use for ambiguous dates with multiple valid repairs; do not use to fabricate dates when no date-shaped token exists.
diagnoses.target_section: Error Handling

overlay.composition_issue: The current skill (image-ocr) covers OCR mechanics (PSM modes, preprocessing variants, confidence) but says nothing about post-OCR candidate arbitration for structured-field extraction. The five diagnoses together form a coherent overlay layer on top of OCR: (1) monetary two-decimal invariant tightens the numeric atom; (2) tier refinement sharpens keyword routing; (3) within-tier consensus selects among same-tier matches; (4) multi-variant arbitration selects across OCR passes; (5) date glyph repair handles the symmetric date-side failure. They do not conflict: (3) and (4) stack (within-variant selection then across-variant arbitration), and (1)+(2) are preconditions that reduce the candidate set (3) and (4) must arbitrate over. Overlay should be added as a new 'Structured Field Extraction from OCR Text' section rather than rewriting the existing Multi-Pass OCR example.
preservation_constraints: Preserve the existing Tesseract PSM guidance and preprocess_image example verbatim.
Preserve the existing JSON output schema and field descriptions in image-ocr.
Do not introduce guidance that implies calling external vision models or networked services; task constrains to tesseract/pytesseract/PIL.
Do not weaken or remove the task-prompt-provided priority tiers or exclusion keyword list; refinements must be strictly additive.
Do not add rules that would turn currently-correct 20/22 receipts into losses: all proposed changes must leave the currently-correct date/amount extractions invariant on the observed evidence.

package_assessment.rationale: The failure modes (74.jpg 702 vs 102, 77.jpg 23.25 vs 23.26 transient, 64.jpg 88.10 vs 88.17 pre-fix, 71.jpg date null, 34.jpg date month ambiguity) all localize to post-OCR text processing: monetary number regex, keyword-tier definitions, within-tier candidate selection, cross-variant arbitration, and date-token glyph repair. Tesseract itself is deterministic given the preprocessing recipe, so the OCR-engine behavior is not the controllable surface; the controllable surface is the extraction logic documented (or missing) in the image-ocr SKILL.md. The source run reached max_iterations=65 and terminated on budget, not on infrastructure failure; model_calls=0 for feedback indicates offline field scoring, not an executor fault. Thus the diagnosis is squarely in the skill-controllable regime, with no infrastructure_or_executor-only components.

diagnoses.label: amount_voting_tier_bypasses_consensus_on_OCR_noise
diagnoses.general_pattern: When combining results from multiple OCR variants, the policy of 'pick highest-priority tier first, then tie-break by frequency' allows a single noisy variant that spuriously matches a high-priority keyword tier to override a value that is consistently extracted across the majority of variants at a lower tier.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: pick_best_total uses min(tier_idx) first; a single variant that happens to match a higher-priority keyword (e.g. 'TOTAL RM' or 'GRAND TOTAL') on a line whose number is corrupted (e.g. 'Visa RM =688.17' being joined with 'Total RM' context, or a blank 'Grand Total' line falling back to 'Cash Received 100.00') is unconditionally preferred over a value (88.17 / 92.80) that two other variants agree on at a lower tier.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: 064.jpg: Variant 0 and 1 both extract tier=3 value=88.17 from clear lines 'Total RN 88.17'; Variant 2 (upscaled) corrupts the same line into 'Total RM = B81?' and 'Visa RM =688.17', yielding tier=1 value=688.17 which wins by lowest tier → final output 688.17 (feedback marks amount_correct=false). 078.jpg: Variant 0 gets tier=3 value=92.80 from 'GrandTota. = tS 92.80'; Variants 1 and 2 upscale into a blank/garbled Grand Total line and fall back to the next line 'Cash Received 100.00' producing tier=0 value=100.00, which wins by lowest tier → final output 100.00 (amount_correct=false).
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Before applying tier priority, cross-variant consensus must be checked: if two or more variants independently extract the same value at any tier, that value should be preferred over an isolated higher-tier value from a single variant, especially when the losing value is sanity-plausible (e.g. consistent with Subtotal/Cash/Payment lines) and the winning value is not.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: In pick_best_total, first compute a frequency map across all (tier, value) pairs and across all values regardless of tier. Give consensus (count ≥ 2 across variants) higher weight than tier index; only use tier priority as a tiebreaker among values with equal support. Additionally, sanity-check the winning value against other numeric signals on the receipt (e.g. Subtotal, Payment, Cash lines) and demote candidates that are inconsistent with every other numeric line.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies only when multiple OCR variants (default / preprocessed / upscaled) are aggregated for a single receipt; irrelevant when only one OCR pass is used or when all variants agree.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not use consensus voting to override a clearly higher-priority keyword match when consensus is only 1-vs-1, nor use it to pick numbers unrelated to any total/grand-total/amount keyword.
diagnoses.target_section: Multi-Pass OCR Strategy

diagnoses.label: fallback_to_next_line_crosses_semantic_boundary
diagnoses.general_pattern: When a keyword line (e.g. 'Grand Total') has no parseable number, the fallback that reads the 'next non-empty line' blindly accepts a number from a different semantic field (Cash Received, Change, Payment) as the total.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: In extract_total_with_tier, when the current candidate line yields no number, the code advances to the next 1–2 lines and returns the first number found, breaking only on an is_excluded() match. 'Cash Received 100.00' on 078.jpg is not in the exclusion set, so it is returned as the Grand Total.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: 078.jpg variants 1 and 2: candidate line is 'Grand Total' (empty number); fallback walks to 'Cash Received 100.00' and returns tier=0 value=100.00. The actual grand total 92.80 appears on an earlier 'Total ... 92.80' line that is never reconsidered.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: The fallback must (a) include 'CASH RECEIVED', 'CASH', 'PAYMENT', 'VISA', 'MASTERCARD', 'CARD', 'TENDERED', 'RECEIVED' in the exclusion set and (b) prefer looking at an earlier 'Total ...' line in the same receipt before accepting a value from a payment/change line below the keyword.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Extend the exclusion keyword list to cover tender/payment lines, and when the primary candidate line has no number, first look upward/sideways within the receipt for another candidate in the same or adjacent tier before descending into following lines.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies to the next-line fallback branch of total-keyword extraction in receipt OCR; not applicable when the keyword line itself contains a parseable number.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not add generic numeric exclusions that would also drop valid rounded-total or 'Total After Rounding' lines; the exclusion must be scoped to payment/tender/change semantics.
diagnoses.target_section: Multi-Pass OCR Strategy

diagnoses.label: last_candidate_in_tier_wins_without_plausibility_check
diagnoses.general_pattern: Within a priority tier, always picking the LAST matching line and ignoring numeric agreement with other lines of the same receipt lets a single-digit OCR glitch on the final line override the majority value.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: extract_total_with_tier iterates `reversed(candidates)` and returns the first parseable number; on 074.jpg, Variant 0 and Variant 1 both pick the last tier-3 match ('Total inel. of GBT 702.00' / 'Total Amt Rounded ——S«702.00') despite the same receipt showing 102.00 on Subtotal, Total incl. of GST, and Payment lines.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: 074.jpg: OCR variants show Subtotal 102.00, Total incl. of GST 102.00, Payment 102.00, but the last total-tier line is read as 702.00 (first digit '1' merged into '7'); the algorithm returns 702.00 and feedback reports amount_correct=false.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: After selecting a candidate number from a tier, compare it against other 'Total' / 'Subtotal' / 'Payment' numbers on the same receipt. If the chosen value is a lone outlier while 2+ other total-like lines agree on a different value, prefer the agreeing value.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Collect all numbers from lines matching any total/subtotal/payment keyword in a single OCR variant. If the LAST-in-tier candidate disagrees with the mode of the other total-like numbers by more than a plausible rounding delta (e.g. > 1.00), prefer the mode value and record the discrepancy as a warning.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies to receipts where multiple total/subtotal/payment lines are available for cross-check; not applicable to minimal receipts with a single total line.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not use this check to overwrite a correct total that genuinely differs from an earlier Subtotal because of GST/rounding (differences within ~10% should not trigger override).
diagnoses.target_section: Quality Self-Check

diagnoses.label: amount_split_line_fallback_consumes_payment_lines
diagnoses.general_pattern: When a keyword line matches a priority tier but no numeric value is extracted from it, a 'split-across-two-lines' fallback scans subsequent lines for a number. Without constraining that fallback to lines whose semantics are compatible with 'the next line continuing the same total', it can latch onto adjacent payment/tender rows (Visa, Cash Received, Mastercard) that share currency tokens, yielding a payment amount instead of the receipt total.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Trigger the split-line fallback whenever the keyword line itself fails to yield a 2-decimal number, and accept the first non-empty, non-excluded next line's last number regardless of whether that next line is actually a payment/tender/change row.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: In 064.jpg variant 2, 'Total RM = B81?' matches TOTAL RM but has no valid decimal; the fallback walks to 'Visa RM =688.17' and returns 688.17 instead of the correctly-parsed 'Total Gross C RM 86.17/88.17' on nearby lines. In 078.jpg, Grand Total line loses its number and the fallback uses 'Cash Received 100.00' until 'Cash Received' is added to exclusions.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Before invoking the split-line fallback, require that (a) the keyword line contains no digit at all (true pure-keyword case per task hint), and (b) the exclusion set covers all payment/tender synonyms that commonly appear immediately below totals (Cash Received/Tendered/Payment, Visa, Mastercard, Credit, Debit, Card). The fallback must not act when the keyword line already contains digits that failed numeric parsing (indicating OCR corruption, not a line split).
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Scope the split-line fallback to the exact task-specified case: keyword line has zero digits. For any other failure to parse a decimal, continue iterating earlier same-tier candidates rather than reading forward into unrelated rows. Also broaden the payment/tender exclusion list to include Visa/Mastercard/Credit/Debit/Card and all Cash <verb> variants, so even a legitimate split cannot land on a payment line.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies to receipt total extraction where keyword/value may be on different lines and payment/tender rows immediately follow the total line. Only governs the fallback branch, not the primary same-line numeric extraction.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not generalize to date extraction, to the primary same-line regex, or to non-receipt OCR domains. Does not justify banning all forward-looking parsing when the keyword line is a true pure-keyword line.
diagnoses.target_section: Multi-Pass OCR Strategy / Receipt total extraction heuristics (new or existing section covering keyword-based field extraction)

diagnoses.label: cross_variant_vote_prefers_frequency_over_consistency
diagnoses.general_pattern: When aggregating a field across multiple OCR variants of the same image, selecting by (tier priority, raw frequency across variants) alone can let an OCR mis-recognition that is replicated across variants outvote the correct value that appears consistently with corroborating lines in a single clean variant. Majority vote is not a substitute for internal consistency checks against supporting fields (subtotal, payment, change).
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Pick the total by taking the highest-priority tier with any candidate and, within that tier, the value with the highest count across variants, breaking ties by earliest occurrence; ignore whether the same value also appears elsewhere in the receipt (e.g., matching subtotal / payment minus change).
diagnoses.observable_evidence: For 074.jpg the model selects 702.00 because two upscaled variants both OCR 'Total Amt Rounded' as 702.00 while variant 2 yields 102.00 (and 102.00 also appears as Subtotal and Payment in that variant). The vote prefers 702.00 purely because of count=2 vs count=1, despite 102.00 having internal cross-line support.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Augment the voting score with a corroboration signal: for each candidate value, count how many times the exact value also appears on non-excluded non-tier lines of any variant (subtotal, payment/cash amount, change-consistent arithmetic). Use that signal to break ties or override low-margin frequency wins at the same tier.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Rank candidates by (tier priority, corroborated_support, raw frequency, position). Corroborated support = count of other total-adjacent anchors (SUB TOTAL value, Payment value, Cash - Change arithmetic) that match the candidate within tolerance. Only when corroboration ties should raw cross-variant frequency decide.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies to multi-pass OCR aggregation for numeric receipt fields with multiple internal anchors (totals, subtotals, payments). Scoped to the voting/aggregation step, not to per-variant extraction regexes.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not generalize to free-text aggregation, to fields without redundant internal anchors, or to replacing tier priority. Does not justify arithmetic reconstruction when subtotal and tax are not both reliably parseable.
diagnoses.target_section: Multi-Pass OCR Strategy (voting / result combination subsection)

diagnoses.label: preprocessing_variants_can_degrade_clear_receipts
diagnoses.general_pattern: Running aggressive preprocessing variants (upscale, invert, sharpen) and treating all variants as equal voters can introduce systematic OCR errors on already-legible scans. If downstream aggregation does not weight by per-variant quality (confidence or anchor consistency), degraded variants can dominate correct ones.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Produce N preprocessed variants and feed every variant's extracted candidate into the voter with equal weight, assuming more variants is always better.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: 078.jpg variant 0 (base) cleanly produces Grand Total 92.80 and matching Total 92.80, while upscaled variants 1 and 2 destroy the number on the Grand Total line and leave only Cash Received 100.00 nearby. 074.jpg shows two variants OCR 702.00 while a third gives the self-consistent 102.00. Equal-weight aggregation lets degraded variants win.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Attach a quality signal to each variant (e.g., average Tesseract confidence, or internal-consistency score computed from how many of {Grand Total, Total, Subtotal, Payment, Cash-Change} agree). Downweight variants with low consistency when voting; or short-circuit to the single variant whose extracted total is internally corroborated.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Compute a per-variant consistency score before voting. Prefer a variant whose total aligns with at least one other anchor on the same variant over any cross-variant plurality that lacks such alignment. Keep multi-pass for recall, but use quality-weighted combination.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies to multi-variant OCR pipelines for structured documents with redundant fields. Does not apply when only a single OCR pass is used or when no cross-field consistency anchors exist.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not generalize to disabling preprocessing variants wholesale; they still help on faded or dark images. Does not justify discarding Tesseract confidence for other fields where it is unreliable.
diagnoses.target_section: Image Preprocessing / Multi-Pass OCR Strategy (quality-weighted combination guidance)

diagnoses.label: Column-header fallback picks first line-item amount when AMOUNT keyword appears inside a table header
diagnoses.general_pattern: When the amount-keyword scanner matches a line whose text is a tabular column header (e.g., 'Description Qty Price Amount', 'Qty U.Price RM(Total)'), the two-line fallback rule naively consumes the next line and returns the first line-item's amount instead of the final total. This causes a wrong, confident numeric prediction rather than a safe null, because the keyword scanner conflates column-header occurrences of TOTAL/AMOUNT with amount-label occurrences.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Treating any line that contains an amount keyword (TOTAL, AMOUNT) as a label line and, when it carries no digits, blindly reading the last number from the next line via the split-across-two-lines fallback.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Window w0008: on 078.jpg variant 0, candidates returned [(3, 20.0)] from line 10 'Description Qty Price Amount' → fallback reads line 11 '"Ty O6SBRAISED 7 2000 20.00' and yields 20.00; the actual grand total line in that image (seen in supplied source image 078.jpg) is 'Grand Total : 92.80'. Field_feedback shows 078.jpg amount_correct=false. Agent trace in a0067/a0068 explicitly diagnoses this and later adds DESCRIPTION/QTY+AMOUNT/PRICE+AMOUNT exclusion regexes, confirming the mechanism.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Before applying the 'next line last-number' fallback for an amount-keyword line, require that the line looks like an amount label (e.g., keyword near end-of-line, no other column-header tokens like DESCRIPTION/QTY/PRICE on the same line, and the line is at/below a summary region).
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Classify keyword-bearing lines into (a) amount-label lines vs. (b) tabular column headers using co-occurrence of header tokens (DESCRIPTION, ITEM, QTY, U.PRICE, UNIT PRICE, PRICE, AMOUNT appearing together) and position relative to a detected summary/totals region; exclude column-header lines from both direct-match and two-line fallback candidate generation.
diagnoses.mechanism_anchor: amount-keyword line classification: label vs. tabular column header before applying two-line fallback
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies only to receipt-style OCR text where TOTAL/AMOUNT keywords legitimately appear both as column headers in itemized tables and as summary labels; relevant when the fallback 'use last number on next line' rule is in effect.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not generalize to generic document OCR where 'Amount'/'Total' columns do not have a trailing summary section, nor to tasks that must preserve line-item amounts (this constraint specifically concerns extracting the final summary total).
diagnoses.target_section: Receipt total extraction / keyword priority and fallback rules (new or within an existing receipt-oriented subsection; otherwise under 'Multi-Pass OCR Strategy' as a post-OCR parsing note)

diagnoses.label: Mangled 'Grand Total' tokens defeat strict GRAND\s+TOTAL regex and prevent recovery of highest-priority total
diagnoses.general_pattern: The highest-priority keyword tier requires a whitespace-separated 'GRAND TOTAL' match, but Tesseract commonly produces 'GrandTotal', 'GrandTota.', 'Grand Tota.', or glues 'Grand' and 'Total' with punctuation/noise. These variants silently fail to match the tier-0 regex and the extractor falls back to lower-priority (plain 'TOTAL') or unrelated lines, losing the strongest signal even when the amount digits were read correctly nearby.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Encoding GRAND TOTAL as a single rigid pattern \bGRAND\s+TOTAL\b that assumes clean whitespace tokenization from OCR.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Window w0008 agent_thought a0070: '"GrandTota. = tS 92.80" — "Grand Tota." — my regex `\\bGRAND\\s+TOTAL\\b` needs a space between Grand and Total. Doesn't match.' Window a0071 OCR dump shows multiple variants producing 'GrandTotal.', 'GrandTota.', 'GrandTotal =', 'Grand Tota.' with 92.80 adjacent. Final predicted amount for 078.jpg remained null after the fix (field_feedback amount_correct=false).
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Normalize OCR label tokens prior to keyword matching (collapse internal spaces, strip trailing punctuation, allow 0+ whitespace between GRAND and TOTAL and fuzzy suffix like TOTA[.L]?), or run keyword search against a canonicalized representation of each line.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Define GRAND TOTAL detection with a tolerant pattern such as GRAND\s*TOTA(?:L|\.|L\.)? applied after collapsing whitespace/punctuation; and/or canonicalize each line (lowercase, remove non-alnum, re-split) before keyword matching while still extracting the number from the original line.
diagnoses.mechanism_anchor: OCR-tolerant keyword matching for compound labels (GRAND TOTAL, SUB TOTAL, NET TOTAL)
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies to compound-word label detection in low-quality scanned receipt OCR; the hint's keyword priority list is preserved — only the matching regex strictness is relaxed.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not relax matching so far that 'GRAND' alone or 'TOTAL' hidden inside a word like 'SUBTOTAL' matches; must still respect existing exclusion keywords (SUBTOTAL/SUB TOTAL) and tier priority.
diagnoses.target_section: Receipt total extraction / keyword priority and OCR-tolerant matching (same subsection as diagnosis 1)

diagnoses.label: OCR variant set lacks aggressive upscaling+PSM 4 pass needed for small-font totals
diagnoses.general_pattern: The multi-pass OCR variant generator yields default, grayscale+autocontrast PSM 6, and 2x-upscale PSM 6, which can still produce heavily corrupted amount digits ('92:80', '92 80', '9280', 'SRT') for small/thin fonts. Without a higher-magnification variant plus a column-oriented PSM (e.g., 3x upscale + PSM 4), the voting pool never contains a clean 'Grand Total ... 92.80' line, so no candidate can be elected regardless of downstream matching rules.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Fixing a short, static list of preprocessing+PSM combinations and relying on voting without diagnosing whether any variant actually captured the summary digits legibly.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Window a0071 experimental sweep for 078.jpg: 'upscale 3x gray, psm=4: [Grand Total a 92.80]'; agent in a0072 recognises this specific variant is needed; a0073 then adds a big3+psm 4 variant. Prior pipeline (a0066/a0069) with only the three original variants produced [] candidates in variants 1 and 2 and only the mis-matched 20.00 in variant 0.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: When a receipt image's summary region is small or thin-printed, treat preprocessing/PSM as a tunable search space and include at least one high-magnification (3x+) upscale paired with a column-mode PSM (4) in addition to block-mode PSM 6.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Expose a receipt-tuned OCR variant list that spans (resolution: 1x,2x,3x) × (PSM: 4,6, optionally 11) with grayscale+autocontrast, and recommend adding/removing variants empirically when summary-region digits remain unreadable; document this as part of the Multi-Pass OCR Strategy for receipts.
diagnoses.mechanism_anchor: receipt-tuned preprocessing+PSM variant matrix for small-font summary digits
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies to Tesseract-based receipt OCR where total/grand-total digits are rendered at small physical size; costs more CPU per image, acceptable for small batches like this dataset.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not generalize to large-text/high-DPI inputs where 3x upscaling wastes compute, or to tasks requiring strict single-pass OCR; do not replace existing variants, only add.
diagnoses.target_section: Multi-Pass OCR Strategy / Advanced Preprocessing Strategies

diagnoses.label: No cross-variant total-value voting rule documented; implicit voting masks correct minority candidates
diagnoses.general_pattern: When different OCR variants disagree on the total (e.g., one yields a correct label-match 92.80, others yield null or a misread 20.00), the extractor's implicit majority/first-match voting can select the wrong value or null even though a correct candidate exists. The skill does not describe how to combine per-variant candidates by priority tier and label-anchor quality rather than raw frequency.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Window a0066 shows variant-0 produced the only candidate (3, 20.0) due to header-line fallback; variants 1 and 2 produced []. After the header-exclusion fix (a0069), 078.jpg became None because the one remaining candidate was removed and no variant surfaced a legitimate GRAND TOTAL match. Agent thought a0070 notes 'voting picks majority which is 702 from 2 variants' for 074.jpg and that 074.jpg amount_correct=false in field_feedback, suggesting the voting rule itself is a repeated failure surface.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Define a deterministic combination rule: (1) prefer candidates whose keyword tier is highest across all variants; (2) within a tier, prefer values that appear in multiple variants; (3) break remaining ties by proximity to a detected summary region; (4) require a minimum anchor-quality (label actually matched, not fallback) before returning a non-null value.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Document a tiered-vote aggregation for multi-pass receipt OCR: collect (tier, value, anchor_type) tuples per variant, group by rounded value, score by (tier_rank, anchor_strength, variant_support), return the top-scoring value or null if no tier<=3 anchored candidate exists.
diagnoses.mechanism_anchor: tiered multi-variant candidate aggregation for receipt totals
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies whenever multiple OCR variants are run for the same receipt and must be reconciled into one value; does not apply to single-pass OCR flows.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not generalize to non-receipt OCR where there is no keyword priority list, or to tasks where any detected amount is acceptable.
diagnoses.target_section: Multi-Pass OCR Strategy / combining results across passes (extend existing 'Combine results' bullet)

diagnoses.general_pattern: The agent consumed 65/65 iterations and terminated at max_iterations with the pipeline still mid-fix for 078.jpg and 074.jpg (amount), after adopting a per-receipt debugging loop (trace one image, add exclusion/variant, rerun whole batch). The underlying skill does not steer the agent toward offline/precomputed diagnostics (dump all per-image candidate lists once, then batch-fix) which would make the same reasoning fit within the iteration budget.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Treating each failing receipt as a fresh interactive debug session (trace candidates → think → edit regex → rerun full pipeline), consuming an iteration per micro-adjustment.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: execution_metadata.agent_iterations=65, max_iterations_at_source=65, termination_reason='max_iterations', acp_stop_reason='max_turn_requests'. Window a0074 explicitly records MaxIterationsReached. Multiple consecutive windows (a0065–a0073) show single-image iterative tracing/editing against 078.jpg alone.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Before iterative per-image fixes, dump a single aggregated diagnostic artifact listing, for every image: per-variant OCR text slice around keywords, candidate tier/value/anchor, and current prediction; then plan a small set of pattern/variant edits that address multiple images together.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Recommend a 'batch diagnostic snapshot then batch edit' workflow in the receipt-OCR section: one pass to build a per-image candidate report, then a single consolidated change set, then one re-run — rather than one re-run per image.
diagnoses.mechanism_anchor: batch-diagnostic-then-batch-edit workflow for OCR extraction tasks
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies to batch OCR extraction tasks over N images where per-image interactive debugging is likely to exhaust iteration budgets; the budget itself is infrastructure, but the workflow guidance is skill-controllable.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not frame the iteration cap itself as a skill defect; do not forbid interactive debugging for genuinely singular hard images once budget is known to be sufficient.

overlay.primary_anchor: amount-keyword line classification: label vs. tabular column header before applying two-line fallback
overlay.composition_issue: The current image-ocr SKILL.md stops at generic Tesseract/pytesseract usage, preprocessing, and PSM guidance; it has no section on receipt-specific total extraction, keyword-priority matching, OCR-tolerant compound-label matching, column-header vs. label disambiguation, two-line fallback safety rules, or multi-variant candidate aggregation. All five diagnosed mechanisms are additive and share one receipt-oriented subsection; they should be composed as a single new 'Receipt Total Extraction' subsection with explicit anchors so later edits strengthen rather than duplicate rules.
preservation_constraints: Preserve the hint's keyword priority tiers verbatim (GRAND TOTAL > TOTAL RM/TOTAL: RM > TOTAL AMOUNT > TOTAL/AMOUNT/TOTAL DUE/AMOUNT DUE/BALANCE DUE/NETT TOTAL/NET TOTAL) and exclusion keywords list.
Preserve the hint's split-across-two-lines fallback as the default, but gate it behind the new label-vs-header classifier.

Do not remove or rewrite existing generic sections (Basic OCR, Confidence, PSM options, Preprocessing, Multi-Pass, Error Handling, Limitations, Version History); only add a new subsection and a short cross-reference bullet in Multi-Pass OCR Strategy.
Do not add task-specific values (e.g., specific receipt filenames, specific totals like 92.80) or any content that leaks reference answers.
Keep all code examples language-agnostic to the receipt domain (do not hardcode currency or locale beyond what the task hint already specifies, e.g., RM and 1,234.56 comma format).

package_assessment.rationale: Four of the five observed failure mechanisms (header-vs-label disambiguation, OCR-tolerant compound-label matching, receipt-tuned preprocessing+PSM matrix, tiered multi-variant aggregation) are purely text-processing/configuration rules that live naturally in image-ocr/SKILL.md and would deterministically change the extractor's behavior on the observed evidence without needing new tools, models, or infrastructure. The fifth (iteration-budget exhaustion) is partly infrastructure, but the proximate cause observed in the trajectory — a per-image interactive debug loop — is addressable by skill-level workflow guidance ('batch diagnostic snapshot then batch edit'). No diagnosis depends on hidden gold answers; each is anchored to explicit trajectory evidence (candidate traces, OCR variant dumps, agent thoughts, field_feedback booleans) and to visible content in the supplied source images (e.g., 'Description Qty Price Amount' header line and 'Grand Total : 92.80' summary line in 078.jpg).
